title: Do It Again with re-
objectives: I can tell that re- means again.
I can add re- to a word I know to make a new word.
I can use words like reread, retell, and rewrite when I work.
I can use recycle and reuse to tell how to help our planet.
rationale: Each of the eight words is a verb children already know plus re-, so they learn that re- means again and can use it to build and understand new words. Four words are about reading and writing work (reread, retell, rewrite, redo), two are about building and filling (rebuild, refill), and two are about using materials again (reuse, recycle). Children practice by saying the base word first, then adding re- and telling what is done again. The unit connects to the unit on un- from grade 1, so children see that small word parts change meaning.

passage.title: The Box Robot
paras: Our class used old boxes to make a robot, but it fell down, so we had to rebuild it. We reread the directions and decided to redo the legs.
Kai refilled the glue, and Lia rewrote the sign. We recycled the leftover paper and reused the tape. Then we could retell how we made it.

qs.q: What does "rebuild" mean in the story?
qs.why: The robot fell down, so the class built it again.
The story says Lia rewrote the sign.

qs.q: What did the class do with the leftover paper?
qs.why: The story says they recycled the leftover paper.

teacher.overview: Children learn that re- means again and use it with eight words they know. Say the base word first, then add re-, then act it out. The unit ends with recycle and reuse so children connect word parts to real choices. Revisit reply, notice, and float when they retell and rewrite their notes.

notes.va.redo.v: Redo is do plus re-. Start with the base word do. Children may say redone or redid; both are right. Use with real tasks, such as a drawing or a puzzle.
notes.va.reread.v: Reread has the same spelling in past and present; the sound changes. Use as a reading strategy. Ask children what they notice when they reread.
notes.va.retell.v: Retell is not reading the story again; it is saying it in your own words. Use a beginning, middle, and end chart. Past form is retold.
notes.va.rewrite.v: Rewrite is write plus re-. Past form is rewrote, and past participle is rewritten. Use with a short sentence, not a whole page.
notes.va.rebuild.v: Rebuild is build plus re-. Past form is rebuilt. Use blocks and let the tower fall on purpose.
notes.va.reuse.v: Reuse is use plus re-. Show a jar, a bag, a box. Link to saving things. Pronounce the verb with a Z sound: ree-YOOZ.
notes.va.refill.v: Refill is fill plus re-. Use a water bottle at a fountain. Children may confuse refill with fill; remind that re- means again.
notes.va.recycle.v: Recycle means to make old things into new things. Careful: reuse and recycle are different. Re- means again, and cycle means a circle of steps that repeat.

teacher.model: Think-aloud: 'The word is rebuild. I see re- at the front and build after it. Re- means again, and build means to put parts together. So rebuild means to put the parts together again.'
discuss: What words could we make by adding re- to a word we know?
Which re- word do you use most often?
misconceptions: Children may think re- means back, as in return. Here it means again.
Some children think every word that starts with re has the prefix re-; for example, read or red do not.
Children may confuse reuse and recycle. Reuse uses the same thing again; recycle makes it into something new.
extend: Make a re- word wall with a picture and a sentence for each word.
Sort words into ones that do and do not have re- as a prefix: reread, red, rebuild, rest.
teacher.reviewAdvice: Revisit reply, notice, and float: reply again, notice and retell, and see whether a boat floats again after a rebuild.

wida.oral: Say a short word like do, read, or tell. Your partner adds re- and says what it means, then uses it in a sentence.

needsReview: Spanish glosses (rehacer, releer, volver a contar, reescribir, reconstruir, reutilizar, rellenar, reciclar) not reviewed by a native speaker; Spanish uses re- as well, which helps cognate learners.
recycle is analyzed as re- + cycle (a circle of steps that repeat); that is the standard word-part analysis and the unit calls cycle a base.
